title: Govern the Vendor Master with an Unknown Payee
scenario: It is 10:00 AM. Four of the five invoices are from vendors on file - but INV-59004 is from Sierra Tooling (V-1205), and that vendor is not in the master. No banking, no remit-to, no owner sign-off. Read the vendor master as governed data and decide what an unknown payee means for the run.
input: V-1042 Northwind Fasteners - active, ACH ...4021, owned by Vendor Relations Desk. V-1108 Cascade Packaging - active, ACH ...7735, owned by Vendor Relations Desk. Today's batch also references V-1205 Sierra Tooling on INV-59004 - there is NO record for V-1205 in the master.
instructions: Read the vendor master as governed reference data, not a lookup table.
Identify what is missing for V-1205 and why that blocks payment.
Answer the governance questions and validate to mint the vendor record.

questions.prompt: INV-59004 is from V-1205, which is not in the vendor master. What does that mean for paying it?

options.text: Pay it anyway - the invoice has a total and a PO
It cannot be paid yet - there is no banking or remit-to on file to pay to
Route it through the tolerance check to decide

questions.explain: Without a master record there is no verified account to send money to. An unknown payee is a hard stop, not a close call - you cannot pay someone the desk cannot identify.

questions.prompt: Is an unknown vendor a tolerance judgement like a price variance?

options.text: Yes - run it through the 2% / $25 band
No - tolerance is about price; a missing vendor is a missing payee, a different kind of block
Yes - if the amount is small enough, pay it

questions.explain: Not every exception is a number. Tolerance answers 'is the price close enough?' The vendor master answers 'do we know who to pay?' A missing payee blocks payment regardless of the amount.

questions.prompt: Who may add V-1205 to the master so INV-59004 can eventually pay?

options.text: The AP Clerk, on the spot, to keep the run moving
The Vendor Relations Desk, which owns and governs vendor records

questions.explain: Vendor records are governed master data. Only the Vendor Relations Desk may onboard a vendor, verify its banking, and log the change - which is exactly what fraud controls depend on.

questions.prompt: Which downstream step will hold INV-59004 because of the missing vendor?

options.text: The Exception Queue, which routes it to Vendor Relations
The Payment Run, which pays it and flags it later

questions.explain: The match decision routes an unknown-vendor invoice to the Exception Queue, where it is handed to Vendor Relations to onboard the vendor before it can ever be paid.

artifactOnPass.unknownPayeeRule: cannot pay - no banking or remit-to on file

copilotPrompt: Read a vendor master where one invoice references a vendor (V-1205) that has no record. Explain why an unknown payee blocks payment, why it is not a tolerance judgement, who may onboard the vendor, and which step holds the invoice.
successMessage: Vendor master governed. The unknown payee is a hard stop routed to Vendor Relations, not a price call.

intro.heading: Before you match: the vendor record is the payee

sections.title: Master data answers 'who do we pay?'
sections.body: The vendor master is the governed record of who Beacon is allowed to pay and to which account. It is not a convenience lookup - it is the control that stops money going to an unverified payee.

sections.title: An unknown vendor is a hard stop
sections.body: INV-59004 references V-1205, which is not on file. There is no verified banking to pay to, so the invoice cannot be paid regardless of its amount or PO. This is a different failure mode than a price that is a little high.

sections.title: Only the owner may onboard
sections.body: Adding a vendor is governed: the Vendor Relations Desk verifies and logs it. Letting anyone add a payee mid-run is exactly how fraudulent payments slip through, which is why the desk routes the invoice out instead of paying it.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd match the invoice's vendor to your official vendor list and add or correct the master record if it is new or stale.

bestFit.how: a Dataverse vendor table with a maintained-by-Finance form, not a spreadsheet on a share
a database node reading the vendor row, keyed on the vendor id rather than the display name

takeaway.heading: Vendor master governed
points: You read the vendor master as a governed control that decides who Beacon may pay, not a convenience lookup.
INV-59004's vendor V-1205 is not on file, so it is a hard stop - an unknown payee cannot be paid at any amount.
A missing vendor is not a tolerance judgement; not every exception is a number.
Only the Vendor Relations Desk may onboard the vendor, and the invoice is routed there instead of paid.
The workflow can now block payment to any vendor that is not governed in the master.
